details: CONFIRMED by reading: close_fixed_by's planner refuses whenever _branch_live(repo, taken_by), whoever calls; release() works from
any checkout (no worktree check), so "release it from that worktree" is also narrower than the truth. No test runs release then
close. Size: 10 minutes (pick release, fix the message and docstring, add the release-then-close test), or 20 for allowing the
taking branch's own worktree to close it.
evidence: raise Refused(f"... release it from that worktree (relay queue release) and run this again, or close it from there")
lib/relay_queue.py release(): no current-branch check. tests/test_stale_close.py: no release-then-close test.
failing_case: Item taken by wt/x, whose branch has one commit of its own that touches only inert files (a gate log, a check record, the handover).
From the wt/x worktree: relay queue done <slug> --fixed-by <sha> --test <file>::<Class>::<name> -> refused again with the same
message, since the planner never looks at which branch calls it; relay queue done <slug> --test ... there needs a check with Q1 MET,
which a branch without code cannot get (the item's failing case). Only "release" works. The brief asked to decide one and say it;
the message and the docstring offer both.
fix_hint: Decide release: message "taken by <branch>, which is not merged: relay queue release <slug>, then run this again"; docstring and
rules/queue.md to match; one test that releases and then closes.
pass_cases: Item taken by a live branch wt/live, close_fixed_by from the main checkout: refused; the message names wt/live and relay queue release, and names no other path that would refuse again.
Either: after relay queue release <slug>, close_fixed_by closes it (state done, taken_by none, fixed_by the sha).
Or (if the decision is "close from there"): close_fixed_by run from the wt/live worktree on its own taken item closes it on master.
A branch at master with no commit of its own still closes here keeping its take (today's test_q1_a_fix_taken_by_a_branch_without_code_...).
findings.summary: an item taken by a live branch is refused with 'or close it from there', a path that does not exist for a branch without code
